lessons.title: Four ways to reach the PSTN
lessons.why: The connectivity option decides who operates the carrier, who you call at 2 a.m., and which license you buy.
body: The four options on the connectivity page are Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. The others use a partner or your SBC. One tenant may use all four for different people.
Operator Connect for India is its own plan because the regulatory problem is different. Do not hide an India office inside a UK SBC and call it Operator Connect.
lessons.say: Four options. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. Mixing them in one tenant is allowed.
lessons.fault: One global route assumes every user has the same carrier.
lessons.listen: Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing can share a tenant. They cannot share one careless route.

lessons.title: Calling Plans in practice
lessons.why: This is the option with the least SBC work and the least control.
body: You assign the plan, you receive numbers from Microsoft, and emergency calling in supported countries is part of that service. You still configure emergency locations. You do not pair an SBC for those users.
If a Calling Plan user also matches a Direct Routing voice route, you may send their calls onto your SBC by accident. The policy has to match the license.
lessons.say: Calling Plan users should not inherit a Direct Routing route by accident.
lessons.fault: 911 for a Calling Plan user is sent to a foreign SBC by a copied policy.
lessons.listen: Calling Plans use Microsoft as the carrier. Keep those users off a Direct Routing policy you did not intend.

lessons.title: Operator Connect
lessons.why: You keep a carrier relationship without operating the SBC.
body: The operator is enabled in the tenant and assigns numbers. You need Teams Phone. You do not need a Microsoft Calling Plan, and you do not run the SBC. India has a separate operator plan.
Ask the operator which numbers are service numbers for attendants and which are user numbers. A user number that walks out the door with an employee is a publishing problem.
lessons.say: Operator Connect is Teams Phone plus a certified carrier. I do not also build an SBC for those same numbers.
lessons.fault: Direct Routing and Operator Connect both claim the same range.
lessons.listen: Operator Connect lets a certified carrier run PSTN for Teams Phone users. Do not duplicate it with an SBC unless you mean to.

lessons.title: Teams Phone Mobile
lessons.why: The SIM number and the Teams number are the same number. That is a gift for frontline staff and a trap for a reception queue.
body: Teams Phone Mobile uses a certified mobile operator. The user’s SIM number is assigned as their Teams number. They need Teams Phone. They do not need a separate Calling Plan for that path.
Do not put the main queue on someone’s SIM. When that person leaves, the number leaves. CRM matching also fails if the same human presents two caller IDs.
lessons.say: Teams Phone Mobile makes the SIM number the Teams number. I would not put a queue on it.
lessons.fault: One person has two caller IDs and the CRM matches neither.
lessons.listen: Teams Phone Mobile is for people with a SIM, not for the company’s main queue.

lessons.title: Direct Routing
lessons.why: This is the option when you still own trunks, a PBX, analog devices, or a contact-center SBC.
body: You pair an SBC FQDN on a verified domain, present a public certificate, signal TLS to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com and its sip2 and sip3 partners on port 5061, and allow media UDP 3478–3481 and 49152–53247. Firewall rules must allow the published IP ranges, not only today’s DNS answer. GCC High and DoD use different proxy names.

Users need Teams and Teams Phone, homed online, not in Islands mode. Budget at least two media ports per concurrent call. Microsoft does not support media re-targeting mid-call. Codecs include SILK, G.711, G.722, G.729, and AMR-WB only when bypass is off.

lessons.title: Mixing them in one tenant
lessons.why: The plan page’s own example puts knowledge workers on Operator Connect, frontline on Teams Phone Mobile, contact centers on Direct Routing, and a small office on Calling Plans.
body: Write a table: population, connectivity, policy, who operates the trunk. A contact center on Direct Routing and a headquarters on Operator Connect is a normal tenant, not a compromise.
The failure mode is a single voice routing policy granted to everyone. Mobile users then hairpin through an SBC they should never touch, or Calling Plan emergency calls leave the country.
